title: Geometrically connected fibres of proper maps to normal schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $S$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and normal: every local ring of $S$ is an integrally closed domain. Assume that $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], that every generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] maps to $\xi$, and that the structure map induces $H^0(X_\xi,\mathcal O_{X_\xi})=\kappa(\xi)$ as $\kappa(\xi)$-algebras [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then the canonical map $\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ is an isomorphism and every fibre of $f$ is geometrically connected: for every $s\in S$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(s)$, the scheme $X_s\times_{\kappa(s)}L$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. No Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.
